title: React Native implementation guide
lead: Use the current code to integrate the Expo host, configure the Player and sources, and connect UI, native features and Analytics.

blocks.text: Integrate the existing screen
blocks.summary: Build an Expo development host and connect the native Player to PlayerView, keeping the view and source tied to the current Player instance.

blocks.text: bitmovin-player-react-native exposes the native iOS and Android Player SDKs to JavaScript. This screen accepts HLS and progressive MP4 on iOS, plus DASH on Android. Its PlayerConfig and SourceConfig are wrapper types with fields that differ from the browser Web SDK.
Build the Expo development host

items: Follow Build in an Expo project in the React Native README to build the shared UI and generate an external Expo host. The generator copies this repository’s App.tsx and src. Use a development build because Expo Go lacks the native Player modules. Serving JavaScript through Metro and building the native app are separate operations.

Allowlist com.playerlab.reactnative for both iOS and Android on the Player license. The host uses copied local configuration; editing the repository’s key file alone does not update it. Refresh the external host configuration and restart Metro as described in the README.

items.label: React Native README: generate and build the Expo host

blocks.text: A minimal player in the development host

Replace App.tsx in the Expo development host from the previous section with this code, then set the license key and HLS URL. Player and Source are public classes in bitmovin-player-react-native 1.29.0.

blocks.title: Wait for PlayerView, load a source and release on unmount

blocks.text: Initialize the Player before rendering PlayerView. onPlayerViewReady starts Source initialization and loading. loadSource submits a load request; confirm playback through onPlaying and failures through Player and Source errors. After unmount, no new load starts; pending initialization finishes before destroying the Player. A final, idempotent Source.destroy call also releases a Source that was never loaded.
This component combines the responsibilities of PlayerPane in the app. For editing and reapplying configuration, follow the app’s session management in the later sections.
Connect the current native Player and view

items: App.tsx keeps applied settings separate from drafts. It keys PlayerPane by UI selection and revision; ActivePlayerPane passes the Player returned by usePlayer into PlayerView.

blocks.title: Attach the existing native PlayerView
blocks.text:
<PlayerView
        {...apiEventProps}
        {...settings.props}
        customMessageHandler={uiChannel.handler}
        {...("isFullscreenRequested" in settings.props ? { isFullscreenRequested: fullscreen } : {})}
        player={player}
        style={fullscreen ? styles.fullscreen : { ...styles.player, height: workspace.previewHeight }}
        {...(viewConfig ? { config: viewConfig } : {})}
        onPlayerViewReady={() => { if (active.current) { recordApiEvent("onPlayerViewReady", undefined); observed.current?.viewReady(); setViewReady(true); } }}
        onTimeChanged={(event) => { apiEventProps.onTimeChanged?.(event); if (active.current) { observed.current?.event("timeChanged"); void refresh(); } }}

usePlayer and PlayerView are public SDK features. applied, revision, PlayerPane and onPlayerTouchChange belong to Player Lab. Source loading waits for onPlayerViewReady so the native view exists first. The source-loading section below explains ownership and result events.
Change PlayerConfig and SourceConfig
blocks.summary: Convert form inputs into the wrapper’s PlayerConfig and SourceConfig, validate platform-specific values and recreate the Player when applying settings.

blocks.text: PlayerConfig describes creation-time behavior and services. SourceConfig describes a particular stream and its loading options. parseConfiguration in src/configuration.ts is a Lab function: it validates form text, converts numbers and enums, builds both SDK objects and then applies additional configuration, lists and approved callbacks. Empty optional inputs usually omit the property; entering an empty string is not the same SDK operation as removing a property.
Map the basic configuration fields

blocks.title: Translate the basic Player fields into wrapper configuration

rows: Startup behavior
PlayerConfig.playbackConfig.isAutoplayEnabled / isMuted
Autoplay and mute apply when the Player is created. Both app defaults are off. Use Player.play, pause, mute or unmute for commands during playback.
Buffer target
PlayerConfig.bufferConfig.audioAndVideo.forwardDuration

Finite decimal seconds. Blank uses the SDK default: 0 for automatic selection on iOS and 50 seconds on Android. The form accepts nonnegative values on iOS and positive values on Android. This is a forward-media target, not a guarantee of startup time or memory use.
Adaptive bitrate cap
PlayerConfig.adaptationConfig.maxSelectableBitrate
A positive whole number in bit/s; blank leaves the cap unset. It limits selection among supplied qualities rather than configuring an encoder or fixing one representation.
Media address and identity
SourceConfig.url / type / title / poster
Match the HTTP/HTTPS URL and type. Display of title and poster depends on the Player UI. Presets replace source fields and retain Player settings.
Initial position
SourceConfig.options.startOffset / startOffsetTimelineReference

A signed finite decimal offset in seconds. Start refers to the media or live-window beginning; End refers to its end or the live edge. The SDK default is Start for VOD and End for live. This is separate from Player.seek on the current session.
Subtitles
SourceConfig.subtitleTracks
The basic form creates one WebVTT track from URL, label and language; the array editor supports several. Use an IETF language tag such as en-US. isDefault is metadata; select the track after loading.

blocks.title: Build the source and its initial-position options

blocks.text: The wrapper uses url/type rather than Vega’s hls/dash/progressive keys. Maximum bitrate is limited to 2,147,483,647 on Android and 9,007,199,254,740,991 on iOS, JavaScript’s exact-integer limit. Validation before the native bridge prevents integer conversion and precision loss.

items: Apply validates the whole draft and replaces the Player only for a valid change. A source-only form change also recreates it and reloads from the configured offset.

App stores validated Player and source settings separately. Incrementing revision changes the React key and remounts the Player owner. Changing usePlayer arguments alone does not reconfigure an existing Player.
A preset normally reloads only the source; configured callbacks or fullscreen settings can also require recreation. Theme changes recreate the Player and load the applied source.
Reset draft discards pending edits only. A string or plain object cannot substitute for a required native SDK instance.

blocks.text: Overrides are applied after basic fields and take precedence on the same path. Removing one and applying restores the basic field or SDK default. Lists use one item per line; maps use unique name=value pairs. Source and offline subtitle lists are independent; an enabled empty list clears its array. Fallback ad sources must share the same type and need a supported native ad integration and valid tag. Player.scheduleAd can use an item from the applied ad list.

License fields start empty and never display environment values. Set nativeId only when reuse of the native instance with that ID is intended. The native SDK determines value, OS and source support; an OS-specific field may have no effect on the other platform. Offline operations consume their own configuration, while Cast receiver settings apply at process startup. Allow DVR controls the embedded live seek bar and app quick actions at runtime; it does not change an SDK creation property.
Apply settings and load the current source

blocks.title: Load after the current native view becomes ready

blocks.text: loadOwnedSource is the app helper that owns the native source and its target Player. It prevents an older initialization from attaching to a replacement Player. In wrapper 1.29, Player.load returns void rather than a loading-completion Promise. Load after the current view is ready and use SourceLoaded, Player error and source error events to check the result.

blocks.caption: Applied configuration on React Native iOS. Compare this output after Apply; it is not a live dump of every internal native SDK default.

blocks.text: The callbacks editor accepts JavaScript function bodies rather than JSON. Enable execution and Apply to install edited functions. Handler factories run on Apply and player recreation; SDK callbacks run when the SDK invokes them. Selecting a source preset with configured callbacks also recreates the Player. Code runs inside this app without a sandbox. Network callbacks may return a Promise, while synchronous callbacks must return synchronously. Return values are checked against the selected contract and DRM callbacks require their license URL.
Save and reuse named configuration drafts

items: Edit the settings to keep in Settings, then open Configuration → Saved configurations.
Enter a configuration name and choose Save draft. A duplicate name requires confirmation before replacement.

Select a saved configuration and choose Load draft. Review the Changes section, then choose Apply configuration to recreate the Player. Saving or loading alone does not call the SDK, reload the source or change playback.
Use Delete saved configuration to remove the selected item after confirmation. Saved items remain available after restarting this app.

rows: Basic settings
Source format, initial offset and reference, autoplay, mute, forward buffer and maximum bitrate.
Built-in sources
A preset ID is saved only when its public URL and format exactly match a built-in source. Custom URLs are not saved; without a preset, loading keeps the current URL.
Detailed settings

Explicitly supported numeric, toggle and enum values for playback, buffering, adaptation, live playback and selected UI or tweak settings. configurationProfiles.ts defines the full allowlist. The iOS and Android hosts use separate local collections.
Excluded fields

Player, Analytics and DRM keys; credentials and headers; custom URLs, titles and other free text; subtitles, lists, callbacks, scripts, metadata and runtime resources. Loading keeps their current draft values.

blocks.text: Restoration replaces the saved subset as a set. If a supported detailed setting was unset when saved, loading removes a later override and returns that field to its SDK default. Excluded current fields remain unchanged. Names are normalized to NFC, the standard composed Unicode form, and limited to 1–48 Unicode code points; collections are limited to 20 items, 8 KiB per item and 128 KiB in total. Unsupported schema versions, platforms, fields, types or corrupt data produce an error. A different SDK version requires confirmation after validating the supported fields; it is not automatically applied.

blocks.title: Restore editor data without applying Player configuration

blocks.text: The Expo host stores validated JSON in its private app documents through expo-file-system. Replacement retains a backup because the pinned iOS File.move implementation removes an existing destination before moving the new file. If an interrupted replacement leaves the primary file missing, Recover saved configurations offers the previous saved list after confirmation; it does not restore the draft or apply settings. A malformed primary file is reported rather than silently replaced. These values are not encrypted by this feature and may be included in operating-system backups. No account API or network request is needed to save or load them.
Customize Player UI and React controls
blocks.summary: Configure the embedded Player UI, package shared themes and connect React Native controls and fullscreen handlers.

blocks.text: There are two UI layers. PlayerView displays the native video and SDK-managed controls, which can use Bitmovin’s HTML/JavaScript UI on iOS and Android. The surrounding React Native buttons, switches, settings forms and Modal belong to this app. Changing a React StyleSheet affects those native views; it does not restyle the embedded HTML controls.

rows: Use an existing shared theme
The UI picker selects a factory name in App.tsx UI_MODES. Sports, Live and Cinema resolve through packages/ui-shared/src/global.ts.
Select the theme; the keyed PlayerPane recreates the Player with the applied source. Default explicitly selects the bundled buildSmallScreenUI factory and keeps its stock component layout.
Change the embedded UI appearance
PlayerConfig.styleConfig.playerUiCss replaces the UI stylesheet; supplementalPlayerUiCss adds styles. playerUiJs replaces its JavaScript bundle.
Try the path in SDK overrides and Apply. For packaged assets, rebuild the shared UI and native resources as described below.
Change the UI composition
Edit the selected factory in packages/ui-shared/src/liveUi.ts and its components. Register any new factory in global.ts and select its exported name.
Build the shared bundle, copy it into the external Expo host assets/webui, rerun prebuild and rebuild the native app.
Change the video fit or native view
PlayerViewProps.scalingMode configures Fit, Zoom or Stretch. PlayerViewConfig holds view options; WebUiConfig configures the embedded Web UI.
Search the corresponding path in SDK overrides and Apply. Fit preserves the whole picture; Zoom may crop; Stretch can alter the aspect ratio.
Add an app-level control
Use the React buttons beside PlayerView as the pattern. Connect the handler to the current player and observe SDK state/events after the call.
JavaScript changes can reload through Metro; new native modules or bundled UI assets require a native rebuild. The Code tab uses Expo Clipboard for copying.

blocks.text: Package and select the shared Player UI

blocks.title: Load the shared JavaScript and CSS for the embedded Player UI
Choose the exported factory through PlayerViewConfig

blocks.text: CustomUi is the wrapper class that names a factory in the UI bundle; its name is not a URL. In this app, Android loads file:///android_asset/webui resources and iOS loads filenames from the main application bundle. The native asset plugin supplies those files. A Metro reload does not replace resources already packaged into the native application. Keep the JavaScript and CSS from the same shared UI build.

LiveRewindChannel uses the wrapper’s public CustomMessageHandler. The shared UI sends playerlab-live-rewind-ready through sendAsynchronous; the host replays the latest Boolean text on playerlab-live-rewind-enabled and sends later changes. This leaves the Player, Source and PlayerView mounted, including while paused or rewound. The channel also forwards unrelated messages to an edited demonstration handler. A replacement external UI must implement this optional channel to respond to the app preference.
Configure the native view and fullscreen handlers

WebUiConfig.playbackSpeedSelectionEnabled configures the embedded UI; scalingMode controls video fit. PlayerConfig.styleConfig.userInterfaceType is platform-specific, with System UI available on Apple platforms. isUiEnabled: false hides SDK controls. A React replacement must supply the playback controls and state display the app needs.

blocks.title: Fullscreen and UI messages
blocks.text: PlayerViewProps.fullscreenHandler is a handler object, not a style flag. The callbacks editor supplies a factory with isFullscreenActive, enterFullscreen and exitFullscreen; lab.setFullscreen connects it to this app’s Modal. A matching exit action keeps native and React state consistent. Custom-message factories must return the SDK CustomMessageHandler instance shown by the editor. The Lab context and its owner guards are app helpers, not portable SDK globals.

blocks.caption: The callbacks editor in the iOS app shows a function signature and an explicitly enabled body. Only execute code you trust; the JavaScript runtime is not sandboxed.

blocks.text: Keep keyboard and editor layout aligned

App owns the safe area, so the generated Expo index.tsx registers App directly. An extra SafeAreaView can shift the editor origin and hide fixed actions behind the keyboard. KeyboardAvoidingView uses useSafeAreaFrame’s y coordinate to account for its position in the host. On Android, height behavior can retain the initial portrait height after keyboard use and rotation, pushing fixed actions below the screen. This app uses padding behavior on both iOS and Android to avoid retaining that height. Check button positions against the complete keyboard, including predictive text, in an integrated screen.

rows: While the keyboard is visible

Omit bottom safe-area padding to avoid reducing the editor twice. API panel parents use flexBasis: 0 and flexShrink: 1. Android disables fullscreen text extraction. In short windows or with enlarged text, compact editing hides the preview while retaining the Player.
Compact Source and Player editors

Hide help while typing and restore it afterward. On Android, layout or content-size changes scroll to the end so the entire field is visible, even if native focus scrolling reveals only the caret. No keyboard-dismissing drag is needed. Omitting excess help prevents delayed iOS scrolling from moving the field above the editor. Structured settings, arrays and callbacks remain scrollable.
Selection and scroll position

Keep the ScrollView and Player mounted. useLayoutEffect scrolls to y=0 when the group, field, API view or operation changes; onSelect handles reselecting the current option. Typing and language/tab changes retain inputs and position. Selecting a different API initializes its arguments to that operation’s defaults.

blocks.text: Try tracks, commands and native integrations
blocks.summary: Select tracks and compare quality with the current SDK identifiers, then configure native features, Cast startup and offline playback.

blocks.text: Select tracks and compare quality

items: For subtitles, apply an external WebVTT URL with a label and language. After SourceLoaded, use the subtitle menu or Player.getAvailableSubtitles, then Player.setSubtitleTrack with the returned identifier. Leaving the identifier blank in the Lab input passes undefined to the SDK to disable subtitles; direct SDK code should call Player.setSubtitleTrack(undefined). Play through the cue times rather than checking only that a track is listed.

For alternate audio, load a source that contains multiple audio tracks. Run Player.getAvailableAudioTracks, pass a returned identifier to Player.setAudioTrack, then inspect Player.getAudioTrack and listen to playback. Track identifiers belong to the current source.

For video quality on Android, compare Player.getAvailableVideoQualities and Player.getVideoQuality, then pass a returned quality ID to Player.setVideoQuality. On Android, auto returns selection to adaptation. On iOS, wrapper 1.29 logs a warning and returns without selecting a quality, even though the Lab panel lists this operation. To compare iOS adaptation, change Maximum bitrate (PlayerConfig.adaptationConfig.maxSelectableBitrate), Apply and observe the selected quality and playback. This bitrate boundary does not select a fixed representation.

blocks.title: Call the wrapper’s track and quality setters

blocks.text: one is the app helper that registers an argument input and operation handler. Its callbacks call the SDK’s Player.setVideoQuality, setAudioTrack and setSubtitleTrack. In another screen, obtain the current identifier and call the SDK from your event handler; the registration helper is optional.

APIs runs actual wrapper calls and displays their returned values without translating SDK data. Many reads cross the native bridge and return Promises, so await the value before using it in a UI. A void result records dispatch by the wrapper; it does not establish playback or completion of an unrelated feature. Compare the corresponding getter or matching event for a setter. Player events provides bounded payload summaries, redacts credential fields and ignores retired session callbacks. onTimeChanged also refreshes the app’s live-window snapshot because this wrapper does not expose onDurationChanged.

blocks.caption: Player.getCurrentTime in the Android APIs workspace, showing the submitted call and the SDK result.

blocks.text: Configure Cast startup and native features

NativeOperationContext tracks the current native source and ad lifecycle independently of event-log recording, then checks native getters before execution. Player.skipAd is disabled for missing/negative skip offsets and until a positive offset is reached; IMA is unavailable. For live ads with a positive skip offset, the wrapper’s current-time conversion adds a source timeline offset, so Player Lab cannot establish elapsed ad time and disables the command. Zero-offset ads use fresh native isAd instead of a clock comparison. Query operations and valid configuration, scheduling and recovery routes remain available.

In wrapper 1.29.0, the Android native bridge returns loadingState as the string Loaded, while iOS returns the numeric enum value 2. The app accepts both observed representations. Neither representation records a source/player error, so a separate failure latch prevents a later state read from enabling commands until recovery. Track and quality identifiers are read again from the current source before a setter runs.

items: Picture in picture and background playback require the generated host’s native capabilities. AirPlay is an Apple feature. Check OS permissions, receiver hardware and content support as well as PlayerView and Player settings.

BitmovinCastManagerOptions.applicationId and messageNamespace apply at process startup. Save Cast options for next launch persists the draft independently from Apply; blank uses Bitmovin defaults. Fully close and reopen the app to apply them. Wrapper 1.29’s deprecated BitmovinCastManager.initialize is a no-op, so Player recreation or a JavaScript reload cannot replace startup.

The generated host initializes Cast before the wrapper’s lifecycle listener. Android reads startup state through the native manager’s public API; iOS reports the values supplied at process startup. Saved options, startup options and initialization state are shown separately. Receiver discovery, connection and playback require separate checks.

blocks.title: Offline playback
blocks.text: Use the separate OfflineContentConfig and subtitle list with a stable content identifier. Initialize the manager, obtain options and inspect onOptionsAvailable before starting the selected download. onCompleted reports completion; Player.loadOfflineContent loads the stored asset. Cancellation, deletion and license operations affect the selected identifier. Storage, downloadable media and DRM rights remain prerequisites. OfflineContentManager.addListener replaces the current offline listener. A nonempty edited body requires explicit permission before Run and executes on future matching SDK events inside this app without a sandbox; its inputs include event, name and lab.getPlayer()/getSource().
FAQ and troubleshooting
blocks.summary: Check the causes of playback resets, missing UI changes, subtitle and format issues, and outdated configuration in a generated host.

rows: Why did Apply restart playback?

The form deliberately recreates the Player for changed settings. Applied configuration survives, but the position returns to the source offset. A preset normally reloads only the source; callback or fullscreen configuration can also require recreation.
Why does a CSS edit not appear?

React styles and embedded UI styles are separate. Check the selected factory, the JavaScript/CSS asset paths and the copied external-host assets. Rebuild native resources after changing the packaged shared UI.
Why is a subtitle listed but invisible?

Mark as default does not enable it. Select the returned track, ensure its cue times overlap the media, and inspect source/error events. A wrong language tag or missing URL/label is rejected before Apply.
Why is DASH unavailable on iOS?
This wrapper uses the native iOS Player path. Choose HLS or progressive MP4; a browser’s DASH support does not change native iOS support.
Why can’t the Android player menu scroll?
Swipe within the video menu, not the surrounding form. The video is outside the editor ScrollView; its touch gestures remain with the Player.
Why is the license rejected after updating the root configuration?

Check that the generated external host has the current copied configuration, restart Metro as needed and confirm com.playerlab.reactnative is authorized for that same license on the target platform. Never paste keys into an issue or screenshot.
Why do an API or callback fail after recreation?

They may refer to a retired Player or a resource from the previous source. Query the new instance, use the current track/native identifiers, and inspect the function signature. Recreate player after API experiments restores the applied configuration after destroy.
Why did only the ExpoModulesCore checksum change in a fresh iOS host?

Expo precompiled modules can include generated-host paths in their podspec source and preparation command. After normal pod install, inspect the complete lockfile diff, including dependency versions. A host-specific specification checksum change is different from a dependency update; do not remove the lockfile or alter pinned versions to bypass it.
How are Apply and Reset kept above the keyboard?
Check direct App registration, KeyboardAvoidingView coordinates, bottom padding and parent-view shrinking. The UI chapter’s keyboard and editor layout section describes the implementation.
Why is some help hidden while I type?
Compact Source and Player editors reserve space for the field and fixed actions, then restore help when typing ends. See the UI chapter for platform-specific scrolling behavior.
How does selecting a setting reveal the start of its editor?
Selection changes scroll the existing ScrollView to the top; typing and language/tab changes retain its position. The UI chapter explains useLayoutEffect and onSelect.
Why do settings reset after changing Android's system text size?

When a system font change recreates the Activity, the component that manages an Android screen, the application's screen session also restarts. This sample retains configuration for the current session, so select the source and settings again after the host restarts. Save the applied code beforehand if you need to restore it. Changing the language or tabs inside Player Lab retains the session and draft values.
Which objects can callback code use?

lab.getPlayer(), lab.getSource(), lab.setFullscreen(boolean), lab.Source, lab.CustomUi and lab.CustomMessageHandler expose current public SDK objects or app helpers. No environment or account API values are supplied. Fullscreen factories return isFullscreenActive, enterFullscreen and exitFullscreen; custom-message factories return a real lab.CustomMessageHandler instance. Use lab accessors so a retired Player cannot be called. The decoder’s context argument is the SDK DecoderContext, separate from lab.
What does WebUiConfig.variant expect?

Enter the name of a factory provided by the configured Web UI JavaScript file. The app creates a CustomUi instance from that name. It is not a URL, and accepting a name does not add a factory absent from the configured file.

blocks.text: Analytics / Observability
blocks.summary: Configure the wrapper’s collector and source metadata, then find the corresponding playback sessions in Bitmovin Dashboard.

blocks.text: Configure collection and source metadata

The wrapper’s collector uses PlayerConfig.analyticsConfig, separately from the Player license. App.tsx enables its default analyticsConfig only when EXPO_PUBLIC_BITMOVIN_ANALYTICS_LICENSE_KEY is present. The additional settings form can edit collector options and PlayerConfig.analyticsConfig.defaultMetadata. SourceConfig.analyticsSourceMetadata supplies source-level labels such as videoId, title, experimentName and customData1. Use these dedicated Analytics fields rather than assuming arbitrary SourceConfig.metadata becomes a Dashboard dimension.

blocks.title: Merge configured collector options before usePlayer

blocks.text: In App.tsx, the subsequent usePlayer call passes analyticsConfig into the Player. Explicit license overrides are honored, while metadata-only edits retain the configured default license. Player.analytics.getUserId and sendCustomDataEvent are available in the API panel when the collector exists; neither call queries aggregate results. Avoid personal or confidential data in labels and custom dimensions.
Find playback sessions in Dashboard

items: Use an Analytics license authorized for the generated app and non-sensitive videoId and experiment labels. Play, pause or seek while recording SDK events.

In Dashboard, select the matching Analytics license, period and app/content filters, then match the playback session to the SDK events. Use the shared guides below for metric definitions, aggregation and visualization. Account API credentials differ from Player and collector licenses; keep them in trusted server-side tools rather than the app.
